reasons: F and G are byte-identical in image and JSON, so they tie. Their JSON matches the brief's canonical array (same 2858 air cells, same 16x16x16 size). Their render is the only one labelled 'Front, from south-east' and 'Back, from north-west', which are the two views the render checklist names. The voxel grid makes the 16-cube height, the 10-wide walls, the 12-wide eave and the six roof tiers easy to count, and the path, door and lanterns read clearly. A is clean and accurate (same JSON as F and G) with smooth shading and no labels, so it ranks third; A, B and C are identical files. D shares E's image, which has the same geometry as F but adds a stray black bounding-box line across the model and no labels, and D's JSON matches the brief. E's JSON departs from the brief: it uses a different palette (keys o, i, s, t, x, y), grass cubes in the walls, and different roof and furniture blocks, so its data is the least accurate even though its picture still shows a brief-like tower. The image and the data for E do not agree.
